newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian provinces exceed Q3 lumber export quotas.
newsitem.headline: Canadian provinces exceed Q3 lumber export quotas.

text.p: Canadian lumber exporting provinces have exceeded their third quarter allocations for lumber shipments to the United States and are now facing export fees on their shipments, an International Trade Department daily export report said.

According to the report, British Columbia, Alberta and Quebec have all reached their export limits and are now facing fees of US$50 for every 1,000 board feet of softwood lumber they ship south of the border.
Quebec, together with Ontario, also faces fees of US$100 for every 1,000 board feet, because it shipped more than 650 million board feet above its quarterly limit.

According to the report, as of 0845 EST on Wednesday, British Columbia had exported 77,000 board feet above its quota, Alberta had shipped 207,000 board feet over its allocation and Quebec had shipped 1.8 million board feet above its quota, for a total for all of Canada of 2.05 million board feet.
These exports will be slapped with a US$50 fee for every 1,000 board feet shipped.
Also, Ontario shipped 43,000 board feet and Quebec shipped 524,000 board feet which are subject to US$100 fee for every 1,000 board feet.

A trade department source said exports who had not been given shipment quotas were subject to the US$100 fee for all shipments they make, which he said explained why Ontario shippers face the higher fees.

Under a five-year agreement between Canada and the United States, which became effective on April 1, Canadian lumber shipments which exceed 14.7 billion board feet a year, or 4.226 billion board feet a quarter, are subject to export fees.
Lumber companies who exceed their quotas face fees of US$50 for every 1,000 board feet on the first 650 million board feet and US$100 for every 1,000 board feet for any shipments exceeding that.

Under the government allocation system, lumber exports based in British Columbia are entitled to 59 percent of the total annual quota, Quebec companies get 23 percent, Ontario shippers 10.3 percent and Alberta exporters 7.7 percent. ((Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau, 613-235-6745))
